Dr Elizabeth Macnor

Newtown Hospital

81 Canyon road

Newtown



Dear Dr Macnor ,

RE: Mr Jone Browne,DOB: 25.08.2001

  I am writing to refer Mr Browne whose features are suggestive of seborrheic keratosis or eczema.
Your assessment and management would be appreciated.



Mr Browne is an 18-year-old student , who has a history of facial eczema as a baby and flexular eczema
as a child. He is allergic to pollens and cat hair.

Initially, Mr Browne presented on 01.09,2019 with a tender, weepy and crusty nipple, associated with
surrounding inflammation .The latter was caused by plaster dressing. Therefore, hydrocortisone, soap       Commented [AD1]: a
substitute and Edomine 5 were prescribed. Additionally, he was advised to avoid using plaster, replacing   Commented [AD2]: the
it with mepor dressing and to keep the nipple uncovered, except during sport. Few days later, Mr
                                                                                                           Commented [AD3]: replace
Browne reported that he had responded well to treatment.
                                                                                                           Commented [AD4]: Nine (be specific)
On today’s visit, Mr Browne reported an increase in nipple friction with overlaying clothes, especially
during sport, as well as the nipple never healed. The examination revealed a tender and warty nipple       Commented [AD5]: ; in addition,
despite no crustation or change in appearance . Please note, Mr Browne reported use of hydrocortisone      Commented [AD6]: has
intermittently and wishes a complete resolution of his disease.

Based on my provisional diagnosis of seborrheic keratosis or eczema, I would appreciate your further
assessment for definitive diagnosis and treatment. For any queries, please do not hesitate to contact
me.

Yours sincerely,



Doctor
